page.title: Target
page.purpose: Explain one target completely: what was probed, what it proved, how it is reached, which device-control strategy would drive it, and precisely what is missing when it is unavailable.

priorities.statement: Every probed capability is listed with its result and the time it was probed.
priorities.notes: A stale probe presented as current is worse than no probe. Age is part of the answer.

priorities.statement: Transport is explicit — local host, a named bridge node, or a device-control attachment.
priorities.notes: The operator must be able to tell where work will actually execute, because that changes what can fail.

priorities.statement: A remote target whose host node is offline says so, and is never omitted.
priorities.notes: A vanishing target reads as 'not mine' rather than 'temporarily unreachable'.

priorities.statement: An unavailable target names its missing capability and offers exactly one next action.
priorities.notes: Missing SDK, missing acceleration, and an offline node fail for unrelated reasons and each needs its own remedy.

elements.name: Target disposition
elements.description: The closed-vocabulary disposition for this target, carrying a text label as well as a status colour.

elements.name: Probed capabilities
elements.description: One entry per probed prerequisite with its individual result.

elements.name: Probed at
elements.description: When the capability snapshot was taken.

elements.name: Missing capability
elements.description: The specific prerequisite that is absent, named rather than generalised.

elements.name: Next action
elements.description: The single action that would resolve this target's blocked state.

elements.name: Transport
elements.description: Local host, the named bridge node, or the USB/wireless attachment through which this target is reached.

elements.name: Driving strategy
elements.description: The device-control strategy that would drive this target and whether it is semantic or pixel-grade.

elements.name: Lease holder
elements.description: The consumer currently holding the device-control lease on this target, and since when.

elements.name: Device
elements.description: The model, serial, and Android version of an attached physical device, and the host node it is attached to.

states.description: A fully available local emulator target.
The capability snapshot is being fetched; no results are asserted yet.
The target has never been probed. Explains that no snapshot exists rather than showing an empty capability list.
Some capabilities were probed and others could not be reached; the unprobed ones are explicitly unknown rather than assumed absent.
The capability snapshot is old enough that it may no longer hold. Age is shown prominently.
The probe request failed. Reported as a failure rather than as an unavailable target.
Android SDK absent. Every dependent capability is unavailable and names the acquisition next action.
/dev/kvm absent or not writable. The target is unavailable rather than slow, because unaccelerated video evidence is unusable.
A remote target whose host node is offline, shown with that exact reason.
The device is healthy and fully capable, but another consumer holds its device-control lease. Availability is a scheduling fact here, not a capability gap.
A physical phone attached over USB to a host node, authorized and driven by the semantic strategy. The healthy physical baseline.
A phone is visible to the host but has not authorized debugging. Only a person holding the device can resolve it, and the surface says so rather than offering a retry that cannot succeed.
A wireless debugging pairing lapsed after a device reboot. The device is reachable on the network but no longer authorized, which is a different remedy from never having been paired.

claims.statement: Every unavailable target names both the missing capability and one next action.
claims.rationale: S2A-P0-003. An unavailable state with no reason is indistinguishable from a bug, and sends the operator to the CLI.

claims.statement: A missing toolchain and missing hardware acceleration render as different states on the same target.
claims.rationale: S2A-P0-003. These fail for unrelated reasons; a single generic 'emulator not ready' would make both undiagnosable.

claims.statement: Every capability result is accompanied by when it was probed.
claims.rationale: S2A-P0-003. Capability is a measurement, and a measurement without a timestamp cannot be judged current.

claims.statement: Every target names the transport through which work will execute.
claims.rationale: S2A-P1-001. USB and wireless fail differently, and a bridge node fails differently again.

claims.statement: A target names which strategy would drive it and whether that strategy is semantic or pixel-grade, before a run is started.
claims.rationale: S2A-P0-004. Evidence tier determines whether a run can gate a release, so it must be known before the run is spent.

claims.statement: A target whose host node is offline remains listed, carrying the offline reason.
claims.rationale: Omitting it would make a temporary reachability failure look like a configuration change.

claims.statement: A target without hardware acceleration reports unavailable and offers no option to run anyway.
claims.rationale: S2A-P0-003. An unaccelerated emulator runs at 3–5 FPS; its video evidence cannot support a release claim, so offering the run would manufacture a worthless pass. The next-action control is present but must acquire acceleration rather than bypass it, which needs human judgement to attest.

claims.statement: A target blocked by a held device-control lease names the holder and offers a next action rather than reporting a bare unavailable.
claims.rationale: S2A-P0-004. A device is a single-occupancy resource. Without the holder named, contention is indistinguishable from a broken probe, and the operator goes looking for a fault that does not exist.

claims.statement: A target that is merely leased elsewhere renders distinguishably from one that is free and ready.
claims.rationale: S2A-P0-004. A busy device becomes available by waiting; an incapable one never does. Collapsing them turns a queue into a phantom capability gap.

claims.statement: Every physical-device target names the device and the transport through which it is reached.
claims.rationale: S2A-P0-003. A phone is reachable only through a host node, and more than one may be attached. An unidentified physical row cannot be acted on, because the operator cannot tell which handset on the desk it refers to.

claims.statement: A physical target blocked on device authorization names the missing authorization and states the action to take on the handset itself.
claims.rationale: S2A-P0-003. Only a person holding the phone can accept a debugging prompt. An action rendered as a retry button implies the host can resolve it and produces a loop instead of a fix.

claims.statement: A physical-device target renders distinguishably from an emulator target.
claims.rationale: S2A-P0-003. They fail for unrelated reasons, carry different evidence weight, and only one of them can be recreated on demand.

claims.statement: A lapsed wireless pairing renders distinguishably from a device that has never authorized debugging.
claims.rationale: S2A-P1-001. One needs a re-pair over the network, the other needs a prompt accepted on the handset. A single generic authorization error makes both undiagnosable.
